overview: Black plays the a-pawn first, with ideas of ...Ra6 and a rook lift or of a later ...e5 and ...d5. White simply takes the centre with d4, Nc3 and Nf3 and is a tempo up. The move gains little and wastes time; it is played for surprise.

white_ideas.idea: Occupy the centre with d4, Nf3 and Nc3, and develop naturally.
Gain space on the queenside by playing a4 and Bb5 ideas.

black_ideas.idea: Play ...Ra6 to swing the rook into play, then ...e5 or ...d5.
Transpose to a modern or Pirc set-up after ...d6 and ...g6.

typical_structures.structure: White classical centre on d4 and e4 against a Black set-up with an advanced a-pawn.

character.notes: Black's move is slow and mainly a surprise; no forcing theory.

soundness.notes: Wastes a tempo and not on the engines' list of good moves; White gets a comfortable edge.

structure.notes: Not yet defined; Black has no centre pawn and the set-up is up for grabs.

approach.notes: Hardly played by strong players; a surprise.

level.notes: Little to learn, but not recommended.

sublines_that_differ.name: Corn Stalk with ...Ra6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black aims at a rook lift.

character.reason: Quiet, slightly passive play with no forcing lines.

soundness.reason: A wasted tempo that strong players do not consider fully sound.

structure.reason: The centre is not defined after the first moves.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever play it.

level.reason: Dubious, so not beginner, and little to master.

plans.reason: No clear plan from the list.
